title: Protocol to record and quantify the intracellular pH in contracting cardiomyocytes
protocol: Preheat the water bath of the Langendorff apparatus to 37°C.
Start the Perfusion solution flow in the perfusion system of the Langendorff apparatus.
Anesthetize adult mice (both male and female, 12–16 weeks) with an intraperitoneal injection of 80 mg/kg ketamine and 5 mg/kg xylazine.
Assess the level of anesthesia by firm toe pinch.
Inject 300 USP units of sodium heparin intraperitoneally.
Perform a midline thoracotomy and excise the heart.
Transfer the heart to a petri dish containing Perfusion solution.
Trim the connective tissues using a fine scissor.
Cannulate the heart through the aorta onto a Langendorff apparatus prefilled with Perfusion solution, avoiding aortic valve damage during cannulation.
Start the electrical perfusion pump with a lower flow rate to initiate perfusion with the Perfusion solution at 37°C.
Monitor the pressure value on the connected pressure monitor.
Monitor the perfusion pressure increasing to a steady value.
Observe the dripping of the perfusion solution from the apex of the heart.
If the pressure keeps rising and no solution drips, suspect aortic valve damage indicating retrograde perfusion failure.
Wash out the blood by perfusing with solution for 3 min.
Adjust the perfusion speed to a flow rate of about 4–6 mL/min.
Control the initial pressure at approximately 60 mmHg using a pressure monitor.
Switch the perfusion solution to one containing collagenase type II (1 mg/mL) for tissue digestion.
Monitor perfusion pressure continuously during tissue digestion with collagenase type II for 15-20 minutes.
Check heart surface color and tissue softness to assess digestion level.
Remove digested heart from perfusion apparatus when it is soft, dilated, and yellowish in appearance.
Transfer the heart to a petri dish containing Stop solution.
Dissect ventricles and atria, mince them, and pipette into solution for mechanical dissociation of tissue.
Filter the cell-containing solution through a nylon mesh cell strainer (100 μm).
Collect cells in 15 mL tubes and wait for cells to settle at the bottom of the tube (5-10 minutes).
Carefully remove supernatant without disturbing cell pellets.
Restore Ca2+ concentration stepwise by adding 5 mL of restoration solution with 0.2, 0.5, or 1 mM Ca2+.
Resuspend cell pellet after addition of restoration solution and incubate at 37°C for 10-15 minutes.
Repeat steps involving removal of supernatant and resuspension of cells.
Store cell in Ca2+ restoration solution containing 1 mM Ca2+ at a temperature between 21°C and 22°C for recording.
Assess cell viability by observing morphological changes and contractility response to electrical stimulations.
Use a flat board tip forceps to touch the heart surface to test its softness.
Install a piece of 25 × 25 mm No. 1 micro cover glass in the FHD Microscope Chamber.
Place and clip the chamber on the stage of an inverted microscope.
Connect the temperature-controlled gravity-driven perfusion system to the recording chamber.
Connect the Myopacer Cell Stimulator to the recording chamber.
Set and test the solution flow rate at 4–5 mL/min.

Test and monitor the temperature of the recording solution in the chamber (36°C–37°C for physiological temperature or 21°C–22°C for room temperature) during perfusion by pre-setting the temperature for the in-line solution heater.
Install the emission filter cube for pHrodo Green or SNARF-1 imaging on the Cell Framing Adapter.
Choose the excitation filters by rotating and positioning the filter wheel on the microscope.
Turn on the power of the microscope.
Turn on the power of the IonOptix system.
Turn on the power of the Myopacer Cell Stimulator.
Turn on the computer.
Run IonWizard software (IonOptix, MA, USA).

Incubate cardiomyocytes in a 1.5 or 2 mL Eppendorf tube with HEPES-buffered Ca2+-free Tyrode’s solution containing either 5 μM SNARF-1 AM or 5 μM pHrodo Green for 5 minutes at a temperature between 21°C and 22°C.
Remove the loading solution after incubation.
Wash cardiomyocytes twice using HEPES-buffered Ca2+-free Tyrode’s solution.
Resuspend the cells in the washing solution.
Seed cardiomyocytes in the recording chamber with an appropriate density to identify single cells, allowing them to settle and attach for 5 minutes.
Add cardiomyocytes incrementally to achieve the desired cell density.
Wash-in Ca2+-free Tyrode's solution containing either 5 μM SNARF-1 AM or 5 μM pHrodo Green and incubate for 2–3 minutes.
Remove excess loading solution using HCO3--buffered Tyrode’s solution gassed with 5% CO2 and 95% O2.
Incubate cardiomyocytes in TMRM solution (5 nM) for 30 min at 37°C.
Wash out the TMRM loading solution using HEPES-buffered Ca2+-free Tyrode’s solution.
Incubate the cells in pHrodo Green loading solution for 5, 10 and 30 minutes.
Load cardiomyocytes with both TMRM and pHrodo Green dyes.
Observe merged images of TMRM and pHrodo Green dye at 5 minutes.
Record relatively weaker green signal from cytosol compared to strong background signal.
Detect integrated weak pHrodo Green signal from the whole cell using PMT of IonOptix system in recording solutions without dyes.
Demonstrate pHrodo Green dye loading into cytosol with strong red TMRM signal at 5 minutes.
Observe changes over time as more pHrodo Green dye loads into cytosol and mitochondria.
Record yellow color regions indicating significant loading of pHrodo Green into the mitochondria at 30 minutes.
Control the timing of dye loading by Method A carefully.
Remove and wash out the dye solution after loading, accounting for extra time required.
Use less volume of dye loading solution to reduce cost.
Perform dye loading by Method B quickly due to its fast perfusion rate.
Prepare a large amount of dye solution for Method B as it requires more volume.
Wash the perfusion tube thoroughly with dye solution after use in Method B.
Control the dye loading time carefully, typically limiting it to 5 minutes.
Reduce dye concentration to prevent excessive loading into intracellular organelles.
Pre-treat cover glass with 0.1% (w/v) poly-L-lysine for 30 min if cardiomyocytes do not adhere well.
Seed dye-loaded cardiomyocytes on the pre-treated cover glass in the recording chamber at an appropriate density to identify individual cells.
Perfuse cells with a gravity-driven solution perfusion system at a rate of 4–5 mL/min.
Control the temperature and solution exchange by pre-testing perfusion tube diameters and flow speed.
Illuminate cells using bright field light under the microscope.
Check cell quality under the microscope.
Select 63× oil or 40× oil lens for imaging.
Apply continuous square bipolar pulse stimulation with a 2 ms pulse-width and 10 V amplitude at 0.5 Hz frequency using Myopacer Cell Stimulator.
Check the beating status of cardiomyocytes to identify healthy cells for pH recording.
Stop the stimulation and pacing.
Select a single cardiomyocyte.
Move the selected cardiomyocyte to the center of the illumination field.
Rotate the handle on the Cell Framing Adapter to align the cell horizontally.
Move the cell to the imaging frame.
Adjust the four edge positions of the frame to include the whole relaxed cell completely in the frame for imaging.
Switch the bright field illumination filter to the red filter position.
Switch the light path to the camera via the side port of the microscope.
Start a new experiment using IonWizard software for pH measurement.
Choose the experimental setting that uses the hardware configured in the task manager, including excitation wavelength and calibration parameters for the lens.
Finely adjust the focus on the microscope to see clearly the striation structure of the cardiomyocyte on the screen.
Calibrate the pH by perfusing the cardiomyocyte with a solution at pH 5.5.
Record the fluorescence signal of pHrodo green or SNARF-1 for 3–5 minutes until the signal reaches steady state.
Perfuse the cardiomyocyte with a solution at pH 6.5 and record the fluorescence signal for 3–5 minutes until the signal reaches steady state.
Perfuse the cardiomyocyte with a solution at pH 7.5 and record the fluorescence signal for 7.5 minutes until the signal reaches steady state.
Perfuse the cardiomyocyte with a solution at pH 8.5 and record the fluorescence signal for 3–5 minutes until the signal reaches steady state.
Reverse the perfusion sequence to pH 8.5, 7.5, 6.5, then 5.5 and record the corresponding signals for each step until they reach steady state.
Randomly select another sequence of calibration solutions (pH 5.5, 6.5, 7.5, or 8.5) and repeat the perfusion process to record the fluorescence signal until it reaches steady state.
Move the cell out of the imaging frame and record the background fluorescent signal.
Test for photobleaching by recording fluorescent signals from a single cardiomyocyte without interventions for approximately 10 minutes with pacing.
Record fluorescent signals continuously without interventions for approximately 10 minutes without pacing to test dye leakage.
Move the cell out of the imaging frame again and record the background fluorescent signal.
Test the dye loading efficiency and specificity.
Record fluorescent signals of pHrodo Green or SNARF-1 continuously from single cardiomyocyte for 2–3 min with continuous perfusion of HCO3--buffered Tyrode’s solution.
Switch the perfusion solution to HCO3--buffered Tyrode’s solution containing 50 μg/mL saponin.
Monitor fluorescent signal changes after saponin treatment.
Measure intrinsic fluorescent signal of cardiomyocytes.
Seed non-loaded dye-free cardiomyocytes on cover glass.
Choose single live cardiomyocyte for 3 min recording using optics for pHrodo Green and SNARF-1.
Repeat measurement across cardiomyocytes with different sizes and shapes.
Move cell out of imaging frame to record background fluorescent signal.
For dye-loaded cells, repeat step to obtain dye-induced fluorescent signal.
Measure on 30–50 cells to calculate averaged values.
Choose single healthy dye-loaded cardiomyocyte for pHi imaging and measurement.
Finely adjust focus on microscope to see clear striation structures of cardiomyocyte on screen.
Adjust the size of the sarcomere selection window to cover at least 10 sarcomeres.
Move the window to the center of the cell.
Set the solution temperature control.
Start pacing the cell.
Record the fluorescent signals of pHrodo Green or SNARF-1.
Simultaneously record the sarcomere length.
Perfuse each pHrodo Green loaded cardiomyocyte with a pH 5.5 calibration solution.
Acquire the peak fluorescence intensity value for normalization and proper calibration.
Change pacing rates if necessary using Myopacer Cell Stimulator.
Move the cell out of the imaging frame for background fluorescence recording.
Perfuse the cardiomyocyte with a bath solution containing drugs or chemicals for 3–5 min.
Record the pHi until steady state is achieved.
Switch to control solution after steady state is reached.
Test blebbistatin effects by switching perfusion from HCO3--buffered Tyrode’s solution to one containing 25 μM blebbistatin.
Observe washout effects by switching back to HCO3--buffered Tyrode’s solution post exposure.
Remove cells exposed to drugs and add fresh cells for a new test.
Analyze pHi data using IonWizard, Origin Pro 2021, and GraphPad Prism 9.
Estimate and eliminate the intrinsic fluorescent signal of cardiomyocytes.
Obtain the intrinsic fluorescent signal from each cell by subtracting the background fluorescent signal from the recorded raw intrinsic fluorescence signal.
Average the intrinsic fluorescent signals from 30-50 different cells as an index of the intrinsic fluorescence intensity.
Obtain the dye-induced fluorescent signal from 10-20 dye-loaded cells by subtracting the background fluorescent signal from the raw fluorescent signal.
Average the fluorescent signals from dye-loaded cells as an index of the dye-induced fluorescence intensity.
Calculate the ratios between the intrinsic fluorescence intensity and the dye-induced fluorescence intensity.
Use the calculated ratios to determine the component of the intrinsic fluorescent signal in the total fluorescent signal recorded in dye-loaded cells.
Subtract this determined intrinsic component from the total fluorescent signal in dye-loaded cells for all other experiments.
Correct for photobleaching and dye leakage by subtracting the background fluorescent signal and eliminating the intrinsic fluorescent signal.
Fit the photobleaching and dye leakage process of the fluorescent signal using a linear equation.
Use the slope resulting from the linear fitting to correct all pH measurements to minimize the effects of photobleaching and dye leakage.
Perform analysis independently for cardiomyocytes with pacing and without pacing.
Compare the slope factors to rule out effects of electrical and mechanical activities on photobleaching and dye leakage.
Correct experimental data at 21°C–22°C using slope factors from 21°C–22°C.
Correct experimental data at 36°C using slope factors from 36°C.
Subtract background fluorescent signal.
Eliminate intrinsic fluorescent signal.
Correct photobleaching and dye leakage.
Convert SNARF-1 emission ratio (F580/F640) to a pHi value using the standard calibration method.
Normalize fluorescence intensity signals by peak intensity at pH 5.5 for pHrodo Green.
Fit normalized intensities using a sigmoidal function to obtain the standard calibration curve for pHrodo Green.
Convert fluorescent signals to pH values.
Subtract the background fluorescent signal.
Eliminate the intrinsic fluorescent signal.
Correct for photobleaching and dye leakage.
Perform curve fitting to obtain kinetic parameters using the “Operations/Monotonic Transient Analysis…” menu in IonWizard software.
Average 10 cycles of signals.
Convert fluorescent signals to pH using calibration curves obtained in step 27.
